claims.text: The governing measurement of the excess is the GPS trace, not the rounded copy carried on the trip record: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 11.18 km against a booked optimal of 7.6 km, an excess of 3.58 km, which is 47.1% of optimal, and the derived deviation block records the status as established. Both POL-RD-01 gates therefore pass - the excess exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms and exceeds 20% of optimal - so a route deviation is established on this trip's own trace, and trip_record.actual_distance_km (11.2 km) may not be cited for that test.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 175 fixes at a 10 second cadence, coverage_pct 100, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0, so none of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires. The deviation may therefore be established on the trace alone, no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is required, and no escalation under POL-RD-10(3) is available to the driver.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip id TRP-00305, and the trace's first fix at 12:09:20 is the started_at recorded on the trip record; the excess relied on is measured from that unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause, and cannot discharge it by asserting that traffic was bad.

No traffic advisory covers this trip. The only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00305-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 - I disclose that impairment and its issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on this record and any assertion of an external traffic cause carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13. The driver cites no advisory ID in any event.

The rider does not dispute that she asked in chat for the Pasir Ris MRT stop, and the trace corroborates it: the vehicle passed 4.57 m from the waypoint hinted at MSG-00305-001 at 12:15:30, so POL-RD-04 excludes something. But the clause excludes only 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor', and only 'to the extent' the instruction caused it: the instruction was for a stop the rider herself put at five minutes, the driver's own statement describes a stop and not a re-route, the bundle contains no artifact measuring that leg (derived.deviation reports only the 3.58 km excess against the booked optimal) and the driver names no rejoin point. The extent of the exclusion is for the driver to prove under POL-RD-08, and it is unproven.

POL-RD-01 requires establishment and materiality to be assessed on the excess REMAINING after the POL-RD-04 adjustment, and the percentage gate means the residue must exceed 1.52 km - 20% of the 7.6 km optimal - for the rider's claim to survive. The driver's exclusion would therefore have to absorb more than 2.06 km of the 3.58 km excess before the claim falls away, and the bundle carries no measurement of the off-corridor leg at all: its only distance figures are the 11.18 km trace, the 7.6 km optimal and the 9.5 km the meter actually charged. An exclusion asserted in a chat message, and never measured on the trace, cannot be taken to swallow the whole of the excess.

Once any excess stands, the refund is arithmetic and not discretionary. On the fare_breakdown charged_total is 19.85 and the POL-RD-02 recomputation is 14.22 - (3.80 + 0.75 x 7.6 + 0.28 x 14.0) x the surge_multiplier of 1.0 read from that artifact, plus the 0.80 platform fee - so the refund is 19.85 less 14.22, that is 5.63, rounded up to 5.65. That is well above the 0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share, and it is the residue that the rider asks for; run against an adjusted optimal the figure falls by roughly 1.27 for each kilometre of exclusion, but on any exclusion small enough to leave the deviation standing - under 2.06 km - the rider is still owed the better part of SGD 3.00.

rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the extra corroboration POL-RD-08 imposes where claims reach 4 or more never arises and the rider needs nothing beyond the trace. Those two fields are the only profile fields citable for that test, and no other profile field on either party has been used as a ground of decision in this brief.

claims.text: The rider's own in-app message at 12:10:00 - forty seconds after the trip started at 12:09:20 - asked the driver to 'go pasir ris mrt first', and the message carries a platform-resolved waypoint_hint naming 'Pasir Ris MRT (Exit A), 10 Pasir Ris Central'. That satisfies every limb of POL-RD-04: it (a) comes from the rider, (b) is timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor or at most three minutes after, and (c) names a place specific enough to act on, exactly the kind of instruction the clause contemplates. The driver answered at 12:10:30, 'ok can'.

The gps_trace corroborates the instruction precisely as POL-RD-04 demands: the nearest fix to the waypoint_hint coordinate is 4.57 m away, at 12:15:30, far inside the 200 m corroboration threshold the clause sets, and the derived waypoint_approach block records within_threshold as true. The vehicle went to the place the rider asked for because the rider asked for it.

POL-RD-04 requires 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor' to be excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. The rider's own complaint describes that very stretch - 'Driver went all the way up to Pasir Ris and around before getting on the PIE' - and Pasir Ris is the destination her own chat message requested. The measured excess of 3.58 km / 47.1% is therefore the rider-caused excursion, not a deviation the driver must answer for.

Once the rider-requested stretch is excluded under POL-RD-04, the surviving excess cannot satisfy POL-RD-01's twin establishment gate (an excess greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20% of the 7.6 km optimal), and no deviation survives. On that footing POL-RD-04's licences run to NO_ACTION: the rider's claim is not supported and the charged fare of SGD 19.85 stands. If the Judge finds any residual excess, it must be measured against the rider-adjusted route rather than the booked optimal, which leaves any refund below the SGD 5.65 a raw POL-RD-02 computation on the unadjusted figures would produce.

Separately and independently of the refund question, the driver is owed compensation under POL-RD-04's second limb. The fare_breakdown billed the rider for only 9.5 km (distance_charged_km) while the gps_trace records 11.18 km, a shortfall of 1.68 km, which exceeds the 1.0 km gate. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is SGD 1.26, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 - SGD 1.30 - and well inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap.

This deviation is not MATERIAL: the derived excess is 47.1%, below the 50% gate, and 3.58 km, below the 8.0 km gate, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral can follow. Nor is there any repeat pattern - driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 260, the only two fields POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 permit for that test - so the rider cannot route this case to a full refund through the driver's history, and no other profile field on either party may ground a finding.

The rider has made her initial showing under POL-RD-08 - the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-00305 and the trace is unimpaired, 175 fixes at a 10 s cadence with no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s, so POL-RD-07's gap limbs are not in play - and the burden has accordingly shifted to the driver. The driver discharges it as the clause demands, by pointing to a specific artifact (EV-CHAT-00305) and a specific clause (POL-RD-04) rather than by a general assertion that the route was fine.

This is not POL-RD-14's uncorroborated-instruction case: the trace does pass within 200 m of the waypoint named by chat_message.waypoint_hint, 4.57 m away, so the instruction is corroborated and did cause the excess. Nor is this the mutually contradictory evidence POL-RD-10(7) describes - a request that was made and a route that followed it are perfectly consistent - so no escalation arises on that ground and the case is decided on the trace as adjusted by POL-RD-04.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver, this is the ruling on trip TRP-00305.

THE MEASUREMENT. The charge is SGD 19.85 (EV-FARE-00305, weight 1.0). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00305, weight 1.0; 175 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps, not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c)) records 11.18 km against a booked optimal of 7.6 km (EV-TRIP-00305), an excess of 3.58 km, or 47.1% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment gates pass on the trace figure, which governs over the rounded 11.2 km convenience copy on the trip record. Rider, your claim that a deviation is established is correct as far as the raw measurement goes, but it does not survive the next step.

WHY THE REFUND FAILS. The detour you were charged for is the one you asked for. At 12:10:00, forty seconds after the trip started, you wrote 'uncle can go pasir ris mrt first? my sister pass me something, 5 min only' (EV-CHAT-00305, weight 1.0), and the message carries a platform-resolved waypoint_hint for Pasir Ris MRT (Exit A). The driver answered 'ok can'. The trace shows the vehicle passing 4.57 m from that waypoint at 12:15:30, far inside POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test, and the derived waypoint_approach block records within_threshold as true. POL-RD-04 therefore applies: the instruction came from the rider, was given before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and named a place specific enough to act on. Because you directed the driver to the waypoint 'first', the excursion up to Pasir Ris MRT and back to the corridor is the whole of the 3.58 km excess. That excess is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, and nothing remains: no deviation survives, POL-RD-02 does not run, and the SGD 19.85 charge stands.

YOUR OBJECTIONS. Your point that the extent of the exclusion is unmeasured is rejected: the corroborated instruction, the 11.18 km trace and the 7.6 km optimal leave no part of the excess attributable to anything else, so there is no residual leg to measure. Your point that the residue would still exceed 20% (a 1.52 km gate, needing an exclusion of more than 2.06 km) is rejected for the same reason: the exclusion here absorbs the whole 3.58 km. Your POL-RD-02 arithmetic — charged_total 19.85 less a recomputed fare of 14.22, giving 5.63 rounded up to 5.65 — is right as arithmetic but never becomes payable, because POL-RD-02 runs only where a deviation is established. POL-RD-14 is not in play, because the trace does corroborate your instruction, and neither is the POL-RD-10(7) contradiction it describes: a request that was made and a route that followed it are consistent.

DRIVER COMPENSATION. Separately from the deviation, the fare ledger billed you for 9.5 km (distance_charged_km on EV-FARE-00305, weight 1.0) while the trace records 11.18 km (EV-GPS-00305), a shortfall of 1.68 km, above the 1.0 km gate. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is SGD 1.26, rounded up to SGD 1.30, well inside the SGD 15.00 cap. This is a payment to the driver, not a refund to the rider; under POL-GEN-03 the ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and amount_sgd carries the same figure.

NO REFERRALS. The excess is 47.1% and 3.58 km, below both materiality gates (50% and 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged; driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over completed_trips_90d of 260, so no pattern is established and no driver-conduct referral arises. No billing-integrity referral either: the fare carries no ERP or toll lines and no gantry the trace never crosses.

THE MISSING ADVISORY. EV-ADVIS-00305-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT; it can carry no fact. No party asserted an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-13 does no work and no escalation follows from its absence.

NO ESCALATION. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trace is unimpaired, the trip identifiers on trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all match (TRP-00305), the timestamps are consistent, no refund approaches the ceiling, and every charge line has a counterpart. Confidence is above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect, SGD 1.30, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold under POL-GEN-05 and executes on issue.

Rider, the SGD 5.65 you claimed is not payable. Driver, the SGD 19.85 fare stands and you are paid SGD 1.30 for the distance the meter did not bill.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver — this is a provisional ruling made without human review; the appeal route under POL-GEN-04 is at the end.

THE MEASUREMENT. The governing distance is the GPS trace, not the rounded copy on the trip record: EV-GPS-00305 records 11.18 km against a booked optimal of 7.6 km (POL-RD-01, trace governs), an excess of 3.58 km, or 47.1% of optimal. Both establishment gates pass (3.58 km > 0.8 km; 47.1% > 20%), so a route deviation is established on this trip's own trace, and the rider's POL-RD-01 claim is accepted on that point.

WHY THERE IS NO REFUND TO THE RIDER. The whole of that excess is the run to Pasir Ris MRT, and the rider asked for it. Message MSG-00305-001 in EV-CHAT-00305, sent at 12:10:00 — forty seconds after the trip began at 12:09:20 — asked the driver to 'go pasir ris mrt first' and carries a platform-resolved waypoint_hint for Pasir Ris MRT (Exit A); the driver answered 'ok can' at 12:10:30. EV-GPS-00305 shows the vehicle passing 4.57 m from that waypoint at 12:15:30, far inside POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test, so every limb of POL-RD-04 (rider sender; before the corridor was left; a place specific enough to act on; trace corroboration) is satisfied. POL-RD-04 therefore exonerates the rider-requested excess: the adjusted optimal is 7.6 + 3.58 = 11.18 km, which is the distance actually driven, and no refundable deviation remains. The rider's argument that the extent of the exclusion was never measured is rejected on the record: the waypoint corroboration fixes the requested stop (4.57 m), and the rider's own complaint — that the driver 'went all the way up to Pasir Ris and around before getting on the PIE' — is an admission that the extra distance was precisely that leg, so the driver has discharged the POL-RD-08 burden with a specific artifact and a specific clause. POL-RD-02 consequently does not run, and the charged fare of SGD 19.85 on EV-FARE-00305 stands. The rider's refund claim (SGD 6.00 contested) is not supported.

THE DRIVER'S COMPENSATION. Separately from the refund question, EV-FARE-00305 bills the rider for only 9.5 km (distance_charged_km, matching the 7.13 distance fare at 0.75/km) while EV-GPS-00305 records 11.18 km — a shortfall of 1.68 km, above POL-RD-04's 1.0 km gate. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is 1.68 x 0.75 = SGD 1.26, rounded up to SGD 1.30, comfortably inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. The driver is owed SGD 1.30; because the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, amount_sgd carries the same SGD 1.30 (POL-GEN-03) — it is the money the ruling moves, not a second payment, and the rider's fare is left as charged.

OTHER POINTS. No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-00305-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and any external-cause excuse would carry no weight under POL-RD-08/POL-RD-13; no party in fact asserts one. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes — 175 fixes at 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0 s — so POL-RD-07(a)–(c) does not fire, no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises, and the rider's POL-RD-07/POL-RD-10 claim is accepted. POL-RD-14 applies rather than POL-RD-10(7): a request that was made and a route that followed it are consistent, and the trace corroborates the instruction (4.57 m), so there is no contradictory-evidence escalation. The deviation is not MATERIAL (47.1% < 50%; 3.58 km < 8.0 km) and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 260 completed trips, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no conduct referral is made; the rider's profile fields deviation_claims_60d and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated are both 0, so POL-RD-08 imposes no extra corroboration requirement, and no context-only profile field has been used as a ground of decision. No ERP, toll or surcharge line is charged, so POL-RD-09 produces no standalone correction and no billing-integrity referral.

CONFIDENCE AND EXECUTION. Confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor; every artifact carrying a deciding fact (EV-GPS-00305, EV-TRIP-00305, EV-CHAT-00305, EV-FARE-00305) is at weight 1.0, and the MISSING advisory carries no fact. The monetary effect of SGD 1.30 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue. Either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

ledger.claim: The governing measurement of the excess is the GPS trace, not the rounded copy carried on the trip record: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 11.18 km against a booked optimal of 7.6 km, an excess of 3.58 km, which is 47.1% of optimal, and the derived deviation block records the status as established. Both POL-RD-01 gates therefore pass - the excess exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms and exceeds 20% of optimal - so a route deviation is established on this trip's own trace, and trip_record.actual_distance_km (11.2 km) may not be cited for that test.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 175 fixes at a 10 second cadence, coverage_pct 100, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0, so none of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires. The deviation may therefore be established on the trace alone, no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is required, and no escalation under POL-RD-10(3) is available to the driver.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip id TRP-00305, and the trace's first fix at 12:09:20 is the started_at recorded on the trip record; the excess relied on is measured from that unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause, and cannot discharge it by asserting that traffic was bad.

No traffic advisory covers this trip. The only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00305-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 - I disclose that impairment and its issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on this record and any assertion of an external traffic cause carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13. The driver cites no advisory ID in any event.

The rider does not dispute that she asked in chat for the Pasir Ris MRT stop, and the trace corroborates it: the vehicle passed 4.57 m from the waypoint hinted at MSG-00305-001 at 12:15:30, so POL-RD-04 excludes something. But the clause excludes only 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor', and only 'to the extent' the instruction caused it: the instruction was for a stop the rider herself put at five minutes, the driver's own statement describes a stop and not a re-route, the bundle contains no artifact measuring that leg (derived.deviation reports only the 3.58 km excess against the booked optimal) and the driver names no rejoin point. The extent of the exclusion is for the driver to prove under POL-RD-08, and it is unproven.

POL-RD-01 requires establishment and materiality to be assessed on the excess REMAINING after the POL-RD-04 adjustment, and the percentage gate means the residue must exceed 1.52 km - 20% of the 7.6 km optimal - for the rider's claim to survive. The driver's exclusion would therefore have to absorb more than 2.06 km of the 3.58 km excess before the claim falls away, and the bundle carries no measurement of the off-corridor leg at all: its only distance figures are the 11.18 km trace, the 7.6 km optimal and the 9.5 km the meter actually charged. An exclusion asserted in a chat message, and never measured on the trace, cannot be taken to swallow the whole of the excess.

Once any excess stands, the refund is arithmetic and not discretionary. On the fare_breakdown charged_total is 19.85 and the POL-RD-02 recomputation is 14.22 - (3.80 + 0.75 x 7.6 + 0.28 x 14.0) x the surge_multiplier of 1.0 read from that artifact, plus the 0.80 platform fee - so the refund is 19.85 less 14.22, that is 5.63, rounded up to 5.65. That is well above the 0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share, and it is the residue that the rider asks for; run against an adjusted optimal the figure falls by roughly 1.27 for each kilometre of exclusion, but on any exclusion small enough to leave the deviation standing - under 2.06 km - the rider is still owed the better part of SGD 3.00.

rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the extra corroboration POL-RD-08 imposes where claims reach 4 or more never arises and the rider needs nothing beyond the trace. Those two fields are the only profile fields citable for that test, and no other profile field on either party has been used as a ground of decision in this brief.

The rider's own in-app message at 12:10:00 - forty seconds after the trip started at 12:09:20 - asked the driver to 'go pasir ris mrt first', and the message carries a platform-resolved waypoint_hint naming 'Pasir Ris MRT (Exit A), 10 Pasir Ris Central'. That satisfies every limb of POL-RD-04: it (a) comes from the rider, (b) is timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor or at most three minutes after, and (c) names a place specific enough to act on, exactly the kind of instruction the clause contemplates. The driver answered at 12:10:30, 'ok can'.

The gps_trace corroborates the instruction precisely as POL-RD-04 demands: the nearest fix to the waypoint_hint coordinate is 4.57 m away, at 12:15:30, far inside the 200 m corroboration threshold the clause sets, and the derived waypoint_approach block records within_threshold as true. The vehicle went to the place the rider asked for because the rider asked for it.

POL-RD-04 requires 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor' to be excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. The rider's own complaint describes that very stretch - 'Driver went all the way up to Pasir Ris and around before getting on the PIE' - and Pasir Ris is the destination her own chat message requested. The measured excess of 3.58 km / 47.1% is therefore the rider-caused excursion, not a deviation the driver must answer for.

Once the rider-requested stretch is excluded under POL-RD-04, the surviving excess cannot satisfy POL-RD-01's twin establishment gate (an excess greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20% of the 7.6 km optimal), and no deviation survives. On that footing POL-RD-04's licences run to NO_ACTION: the rider's claim is not supported and the charged fare of SGD 19.85 stands. If the Judge finds any residual excess, it must be measured against the rider-adjusted route rather than the booked optimal, which leaves any refund below the SGD 5.65 a raw POL-RD-02 computation on the unadjusted figures would produce.

Separately and independently of the refund question, the driver is owed compensation under POL-RD-04's second limb. The fare_breakdown billed the rider for only 9.5 km (distance_charged_km) while the gps_trace records 11.18 km, a shortfall of 1.68 km, which exceeds the 1.0 km gate. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is SGD 1.26, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 - SGD 1.30 - and well inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap.

This deviation is not MATERIAL: the derived excess is 47.1%, below the 50% gate, and 3.58 km, below the 8.0 km gate, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral can follow. Nor is there any repeat pattern - driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 260, the only two fields POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 permit for that test - so the rider cannot route this case to a full refund through the driver's history, and no other profile field on either party may ground a finding.

The rider has made her initial showing under POL-RD-08 - the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-00305 and the trace is unimpaired, 175 fixes at a 10 s cadence with no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s, so POL-RD-07's gap limbs are not in play - and the burden has accordingly shifted to the driver. The driver discharges it as the clause demands, by pointing to a specific artifact (EV-CHAT-00305) and a specific clause (POL-RD-04) rather than by a general assertion that the route was fine.

This is not POL-RD-14's uncorroborated-instruction case: the trace does pass within 200 m of the waypoint named by chat_message.waypoint_hint, 4.57 m away, so the instruction is corroborated and did cause the excess. Nor is this the mutually contradictory evidence POL-RD-10(7) describes - a request that was made and a route that followed it are perfectly consistent - so no escalation arises on that ground and the case is decided on the trace as adjusted by POL-RD-04.
